data.body:
I'll work on this. Could you assign it to me?

I'll look at the current code, add a focused test, and send a small PR.

Some context from the code that may save duplicated effort here:

**The sizing part is already fixed on `master`, but not in a release yet.** #11765 (merged 2026-08-28, after v4.9.0 was tagged on 2026-08-20) adds a `cluster` block to `/api/resources` and to the gallery listing, populated from `NodeRegistry.HealthyNodeMemory` — the largest model budget any single healthy backend node offers, GPU preferred over RAM — and `modelBudget()` in the React UI now sizes against that block when present, falling back to the frontend's own aggregate otherwise. The "YOUR HOST" panel keeps showing the controller's genuine usage on purpose; only the fit checks switch to the cluster reading. That should cover the thin-gateway case described here as of the next release, or `master` builds now.

**The "Checking availability..." hang looks like a separate bug and is not addressed by #11765.** That text is just one of the rotating phrases in the generic `GalleryLoader` skeleton, so what it really means is that the initial gallery listing request never resolved once two nodes were registered. I'm going to trace that path on v4.9.0 vs `master` and post a repro/finding here.

@modelpath-dev — since you asked to take this a few hours ago: happy to leave the sizing follow-ups (if any remain once you've tried `master`) to you and focus on the hang, or the other way round, whichever you prefer. Just say which so we don't overlap.

Follow-up with actual measurements. I built both **v4.9.0** (tag) and current **`master`** (`1f2f931f5`) and ran each as a distributed frontend (Postgres 16 + NATS 2 in docker, `LOCALAI_AUTH=true`, `LOCALAI_DISTRIBUTED=true`) with two generic `local-ai worker --register-to …` nodes registered, approved and reporting `healthy`.

**Sizing (the main report) — confirmed on v4.9.0, confirmed fixed on `master`:**

| version | `/api/resources` `cluster` block | `/api/models` `cluster` block |
|---|---|---|
| v4.9.0 | absent (only the frontend's own `aggregate`) | absent |
| master | `{enabled: true, node_count: 2, node_name: "worker-2", total_memory: 8585740288, is_gpu: true}` | same |

So on `master` the fit checks size against the best healthy backend node, exactly as #11765 intended. This should land in the next release.

**"Checking availability…" hang — could not reproduce on either version.** With two healthy nodes registered, the exact requests the Models page issues all return immediately:

| request | v4.9.0 | master |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/models?page=1&collapse_variants=true` | 200, 0.03 s | 200, 0.01 s |
| `GET /api/models?page=1&sort=installed&order=desc&collapse_variants=true` | 200, 0.03 s | 200, 0.02 s |
| `GET /api/models/capabilities` | 200, 0.01 s | 200, 0.01 s |
| `GET /api/models/estimate/<id>` | 200, 0.7 s | 200, 0.9 s |

The only slow call I saw was the very first `/api/models` after a cold start (~3 s), which is the blocking gallery-index download before the cache is warm. That is independent of node count.

Reading the code, the v4.9.0 listing handler makes no per-node calls at all, and that loader text is just one of the rotating phrases in the generic `GalleryLoader` skeleton, shown until the first `/api/models` response arrives. So a stuck loader means that one request never completed in your environment. Two things would pin it down:

1. In the browser devtools Network tab, is `/api/models?…` shown as *pending* forever, or did it fail (4xx/5xx/CORS)? A failure would surface as a toast and clear the loader, so I'd expect *pending*.
2. Can the frontend LXC reach `index.localai.io` (and GitHub as the mirror)? On a thin gateway with restricted egress, the initial gallery fetch can block for a long time before the cache exists, and the timing of that is easy to confuse with node registration. `LOCALAI_LOG_LEVEL=debug` on the frontend around a page load would show it.

If it does turn out to be egress, that's still worth a fix (the listing shouldn't block the UI indefinitely on gallery fetch), but it would be a different bug from the one in the title. Happy to take that one if you can confirm.

Following up on the "Checking availability..." hang — checked egress and debug logs (`LOCALAI_LOG_LEVEL=debug`) on our gateway node just now while reloading the Models page, and couldn't reproduce it this time. `/api/models` came back with `status=200` essentially instantly, and outbound connectivity to the gallery index/GitHub was fast with no timeouts either. Not sure what caused it originally — seems intermittent rather than consistently broken on our end. Will report back with more if it recurs and we can catch it live.
